questions.title: Linear Search First Occurrence
questions.description:
A library server keeps shelf IDs in an array. When a librarian searches for a key, the system must report the FIRST position (0-based index) where the key appears, scanning from the start with a plain linear scan. If the key is not present, print -1.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of shelf IDs.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the shelf IDs.
Line 3: key, the value to search.

Output Format:
One line: the 0-based index of the first occurrence of key, or -1 if it does not occur.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, -1000000000 <= shelf id <= 1000000000, -1000000000 <= key <= 1000000000

questions.title: Left Rotate by K via Reversal
questions.description:
A conveyor belt carries n boxes in a row and must be shifted LEFT by k positions: every box moves k places earlier, and the first k boxes wrap around to the end. Perform the rotation with the three-reversal technique: reverse the first k elements, reverse the remaining n-k elements, then reverse the whole array. Print the rotated row on one line, separated by single spaces. Note that k may equal n, which leaves the order unchanged.

Input Format:
Line 1: n and k, space separated.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the box order.

Output Format:
One line with the array after rotating left by k, separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= n, -1000000000 <= element <= 1000000000

questions.title: Second Largest in One Pass
questions.description:
A leaderboard stores n scores. Find the second largest DISTINCT score in a single pass over the array, without sorting it. Duplicates do not count twice: for example, in 40 40 30 the second largest distinct score is 30. The array is guaranteed to contain at least two distinct values. Print that second largest distinct value.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of scores.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the scores.

Output Format:
One line: the second largest distinct score.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 100000, -1000000000 <= score <= 1000000000, at least two distinct values are present

questions.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
questions.description:
A warehouse stores product IDs in non-decreasing (sorted) order. Compact the array in place with the two-pointer technique so each ID appears exactly once while keeping the sorted order; do not use any collection classes. Print the new length L on the first line, and the first L elements of the compacted array on the second line, separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of IDs.
Line 2: n space-separated integers in non-decreasing order.

Output Format:
Line 1: L, the number of distinct IDs.
Line 2: the first L elements after compaction, separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, -1000000000 <= id <= 1000000000, the input array is non-decreasing

questions.title: Check Array Sorted Ascending
questions.description:
A factory quality checker expects the day's temperature readings to be stored in non-decreasing order (each value greater than or equal to the previous one). Read n readings and print true when the array is non-decreasing, otherwise print false (lowercase).

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of readings.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line: true if every element is >= the previous element, otherwise false.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, -1000000000 <= reading <= 1000000000

questions.title: Prefix Sums of Sensor Readings
questions.description:
An energy monitor records n hourly readings that may be negative. The dashboard needs the running totals: the i-th prefix sum is the total of the first i readings. Compute all n prefix sums and print them on one line, separated by single spaces. Use a long array, because the totals can exceed the int range.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of readings.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with n prefix sums separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, -1000000000 <= reading <= 1000000000

questions.title: Maximum Subarray Sum with Kadane
questions.description:
A power grid logs a net load delta every minute; deltas may be negative. The control room must find the non-empty contiguous window of minutes whose deltas add up to the maximum, and print that maximum sum. Solve it with Kadane's algorithm in O(n), using long arithmetic, since the array can hold 100000 values.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of readings.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, which may be negative.

Output Format:
One line: the maximum possible sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, -1000000000 <= value <= 1000000000

questions.title: Majority Element in the Batch
questions.description:
A quality control station labels each product in a batch with an integer defect code. A batch is dominated when one single code appears strictly more than n/2 times. Find the dominating code and print it; if no code appears more than n/2 times, print -1. Work directly on the array with plain nested scans (n is at most 1000) and do not use any map or set collections.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of products.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the defect codes.

Output Format:
One line: the code that occurs strictly more than n/2 times, or -1 if none does.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= code <= 1000000000

questions.title: Mega Queue Rotation with Huge K
questions.description:
An airport re-queues n boarding groups by rotating the whole queue LEFT by k positions, but k can be astronomically large (up to 1000000000) and far bigger than the queue length, so reduce it with k modulo n first. Then rotate in O(n) with the three-reversal technique. Print the rotated queue on one line, separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
Line 1: n and k, space separated.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the group order.

Output Format:
One line with the queue after rotating left by k positions, separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= k <= 1000000000, -1000000000 <= group id <= 1000000000

questions.title: Missing Number in Zero to N
questions.description:
An attendance device assigns IDs from 0 to n for the day, but exactly one ID never appears in the log. Read n and the n logged IDs (all distinct, each between 0 and n). Find the missing ID with the arithmetic sum formula (or XOR) instead of any map or set: the sum of 0 to n is n*(n+1)/2, so the missing value is that total minus the sum of the logged IDs. Print the missing ID.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated distinct integers, each between 0 and n inclusive.

Output Format:
One line: the missing ID.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, all logged values are distinct and lie in 0..n with exactly one value missing
